assign.request: The two worst-scoring pages on the site that are actually broken: /web/nav/sidebar/ (7/F) and /web/nav/drawer/ (8/F). Dispatched by mastermind-layout.
steps: screenshot both pages, look for real breakage
trace every finding to its cause
verify + write up anything outside the fence

assign.now: reproduced live: analyze(document.querySelector(".app")) matches findings.json exactly — sidebar 1280 7/F, drawer 1280 8/F, drawer 3440 9/F

log.msg: the one high finding on both pages is identical and shared: div.page.flow.page-nav (the hidden .active-ancestor /web/nav/ catalog page) overflows div.pages (the App root scrollport), which has overflow-y:hidden — confirmed live via Playwright: pages.scrollHeight 1998 vs clientHeight 900, window/html do not scroll, .pages.scrollTop only movable via forced JS, never by user input. Not visible in a screenshot — the page just quietly truncates below the fold.

root cause: /web/nav/page.js uses catalog(), so the active leaf mounts two levels under the App root .pages, inside ext/catalog/catalog.js own .page-catalog-pages region. /styles.css hides the outer .pages scrollbar whenever its direct child is not literally .active-page (assumes an inner .pages will scroll instead), but .page-catalog-pages is a different class and never gets any overflow rule of its own from Page.css or catalog.css — only the rail (.page-previews) does. Confirmed systemic: identical high finding on all 11 /web/nav/* siblings (scaled to each ones content length) and on /web/layout/* (the other sessions tree, also catalog()-based) — 18/205 site pages, every one under a catalog. Fix lives in framework/ext/catalog/catalog.css, outside this tasks fence.

verified the fix live via page.addStyleTag (not committed, outside fence): .page-catalog-pages { max-height: 100dvh; overflow-y: auto; } — mirrors what the rail 3 lines above it in catalog.css already does. Before/after (analyze() against .app, matching the site audits own root): sidebar 1280 7/F(high:1) -> 77/C(high:0); drawer 1280 8/F(high:1) -> 82/B(high:0); drawer 3440 9/F(high:1) -> 83/B(high:0). Small residual (45-90px, now low/med not high) remains — 100dvh overshoots the space actually available below the pages own header; left for catalog.css owner to tune.

every remaining low/med finding on both pages also traces to shared code, confirmed by identical values recurring on unrelated /web/nav/* siblings: p.demo-note measure (ext/demo caption(), no max-width — also the sites --measure:52em token sitting right on the documented 85-char edge per the layout-design skill); input.layout-range hit-size + select.layout-pick/demo-tools/demo-dials alignment (ext/layout control bar, identical px values site-wide); pre pad-scale (generic <pre>, framework.css, identical 13px/840px on 8 different nav pages); h4.page-previews-group hierarchy (Page.class.js hardcodes h4 for a previews() group heading — this is actually the hidden ancestors own PATTERNS heading, picked up because the audit root is .app not the leaf); demo-stage.bare whitespace (ext/demo/stage.js, fixed-height miniature, plausible false-positives.md case). None reachable from /web/nav/ — no edits made under the fence.

assign.outcome: **No edit made — the bug and its fix both live outside the fence.** Both pages own content is fine; every finding (the score-killing high one included) traces to shared framework/ext code hit identically by all 11 /web/nav/* siblings and the /web/layout/* tree. Root cause: ext/catalog leaves .page-catalog-pages with no overflow boundary of its own while /styles.css hides the outer App .pages scrollbar whenever the active leaf isnt a direct child — so nested catalog content is genuinely unreachable, confirmed live (Playwright: scrollHeight 1998 vs clientHeight 900, no scrollbar, window/html dont scroll either). Verified fix (injected live, not committed): catalog.css `.page-catalog-pages { max-height: 100dvh; overflow-y: auto; }` takes sidebar 1280 from 7/F to 77/C, drawer 1280 from 8/F to 82/B, drawer 3440 from 9/F to 83/B, eliminating the high severity outright on all three.
